answer: The fable detector writes to mesa, and kernel shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 229 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 101 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 29 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
